request.description: Submit an immutable new version in response to the latest revision request.
Upload a Project Material. Storage consent only: no extraction, embedding, retrieval, or provider call. The first version is created quarantined and is not downloadable until a scan clears it.

item.name: M02 - Upload a Contribution Request Material

request.description: Upload a Contribution Request Material. A Material belongs to exactly one scope, enforced by a database check constraint.
Append an immutable version. The previous version is untouched, so replacing a Material never rewrites what collaborators may already have read.
Owner view of a Material and its versions, including each version's server-authoritative scan status.

Grants read access to a RESTRICTED_PROJECT Material. The grantee must already hold a live Assignment in the Project: a grant to anyone else would never open the Material, because access ends when an Assignment does.
Every grant ever issued, live and revoked. Revoked grants are retained rather than deleted, because who once had access is the single thing an audit of a leak needs to establish.

Ends access immediately, including for download links already issued: redemption re-checks access rather than trusting the token. POST rather than DELETE because the command carries an idempotency key in the body.

Switches the visibility class. Existing grants are left intact rather than revoked, so moving to PUBLIC and back does not destroy the grant list; they simply are not consulted while another class is in force.
Mints a short-lived link for one version. Only a version that reached READY can be linked -- quarantined, scanning, rejected and purged versions have no link at all.

Streams the bytes. The token names the version and the subject; it never carries the authorization decision, which is resolved again here against live grants and live Assignments. The caller must also be the token's subject, so a shared link is not a copy of the document. The path is deliberately not /materials/downloads: that would be matched by /materials/:materialId first, and its UUID pipe would reject the request before this route was reached.

Two-phase. Access ends inside the transaction -- deleted_at is stamped and every live grant revoked -- while content is purged immediately afterwards on a best-effort basis, with a sweep finishing anything storage refused. Audit rows survive the purge: deletion removes content, not the record that content existed.

The supported formats and size ceiling the upload form must state before a file is chosen. Served from the same configuration the validator reads, so the form and the rejection can never disagree; any number a client hardcodes instead drifts the first time an operator raises the ceiling. The path sits outside /materials/ because /materials/upload-constraints would be matched by /materials/:materialId first, whose UUID pipe rejects it.

Access-filtered in the query, not after fetching: a contributor sees public Materials on a published Project, restricted ones only where they hold a live grant AND a live Assignment, and nothing else. The owner additionally sees their own deleted Materials, so a deletion is visibly done rather than a row that silently vanished.

The same filtering for a Request, plus ASSIGNMENT-visibility Materials for the current active assignee. The Project behind the Request is resolved through the owning module rather than by reading its tables.
Read whether an owned Project is accepting Contribution Proposals. A Project with no intake row is accepting; this read never creates one.
Enable or disable new Contribution Proposal intake for an owned Project.
Withdraw a pending proposal without deleting its version or audit history.
Owner accepts a pending proposal, creating an attributed owner-controlled draft Contribution Request. No Assignment, Application, quota, or selection priority is created.
Owner declines a pending proposal with a contributor-visible reason. Terminal and idempotent.
A participant (proposer or Project owner) preserves authorship evidence for moderation. The platform records the claim only; it makes no automatic copying, ownership, or legal finding.
